sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target, unchanged from BTC (20/60/120-day votes, 30-day volatility, 50% target), beats holding the same market at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs, on gold (PAXGUSDT) and on two currencies against the dollar (EURUSDT, GBPUSDT), daily bars on Binance spot.
sections.rationale: Kestrel's one surviving rule has only been tested on crypto, where everything rose a lot between 2020 and 2025; an edge that is really 'crypto went up' would fail on markets that didn't. Time-series momentum is documented across commodities and currencies for a century (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012, 'Time Series Momentum'; Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen 2017): who pays is slow-moving and hedging flows that keep a trend going after news. So this is a test of whether Kestrel's rule generalises, not a new idea, and nothing is tuned for these markets. Stated plainly: gold moves about 15% a year and EUR about 7%, so the 50% volatility target always caps the weight at 100%: on these markets the rule is its three trend votes, fully in or out. That is the frozen rule as it is; a lower target would be a new trial. Luke chose the markets (2026-11-16): silver has no Binance spot market; AUDUSDT stopped in 2023-06 and is too short; XAUTUSDT starts in 2026-03. Disclosure: gold is not wholly unseen. PAXGUSDT 2020-08 to 2025-10 was half of the BTC and gold rotation (dropped 2026-11-15), so its path in that period has been looked at, though never with this rule. EUR and GBP prices were never looked at before this note. PAXG's and EUR's holdout years are unseen, and they are the clean test.
sections.rules: trend-vol-target with its defaults, daily bars, 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fees; each market pays its own spread band from its daily volume). PAXGUSDT 2020-08 (its listing) to 2025-10; EURUSDT 2020-01 to 2025-10; GBPUSDT 2020-07 to 2023-12 (Binance stopped it). For each: kestrel backtest, kestrel walk-forward (grid slow_days 90,120,180 x target_vol_pct 30,50,70; 24-month train, 6-month test, as for BTC), kestrel robustness around the defaults. All before the holdout.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard for each market, judged against the same market held at the same exposure. A market that passes every test except luck and out of sample (BTC's standard for pursue) earns its own holdout note: PAXGUSDT and EURUSDT have unused holdout years (2025-11 to 2026-10); GBPUSDT has none, so it can be recorded but never pursued. A market that fails anything else is recorded and not taken further. If the rule fails on all three, the finding is that Kestrel's edge has only been shown on crypto.
sections.parameters: fast_days 20, mid_days 60, slow_days 120, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50; the walk-forward grid and robustness neighbours as for BTC. Nothing new is tuned.
sections.costs: Daily trend votes: turnover like BTC's (break-even there was 287 bps). These markets are low-volatility, so a trend's gains are small and costs matter more; each pays its own spread band (likely 8-15 bps a side on volume alone, which may overstate EUR's real spread). Trials: three markets, each one run plus its grid and neighbours, about 60 in all.
